How fresh is each section? The competitor comparison, authority, traffic, top-pages, backlink, keyword-gap and AI Overview sections were refreshed live from the Ahrefs API on 10 August 2026. Keyword Rankings was refreshed from SE Ranking the same day. GSC Performance (through June 2026) and GA4 Performance (through July 2026) were not refreshed — neither tool exposes an API for this account, so both sections require fresh manual exports.
AEO note: Ahrefs Brand Radar (per-LLM citation tracking across ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini) needs a paid add-on not on the current subscription, so the AI Overview section uses SERP-level Google AI Overview citation data as the closest available proxy. Competitor set mirrors the SE Ranking rank-tracker project.

Executive Summary

Milepost (milepostinsurance.com) benchmarked against its Tier-1 direct SEO peers (owner-operator / commercial-truck insurance agencies) and Tier-2 category & AEO benchmarks (Progressive Commercial, The Hartford, Insureon), plus two Berkshire siblings the client asked us to watch. All figures are US-market unless the column says worldwide (WW). Bolded cells lead each metric. Headline this cycle: organic traffic up 20% week over week to 231 visits/mo, and referring domains up 39 — almost all of the link growth is spam.

Share of Voice Trends

Each domain's slice of the tracked set's combined US organic traffic, monthly through July 2026 plus a point-in-time reading for 10 August (marked with an asterisk). Progressive, The Hartford and GEICO dominate the stack; the Tier-1 peers and Milepost compete for a thin sliver at the bottom. Read this as relative share, not absolute volume.

Authority Trends

Domain Rating and referring-domain growth, monthly through July 2026 plus a 10 August point. The industry-wide referring-domain spike since May 2026 is the thing to be sceptical of — Milepost's referring domains have gone 50 → 444 since April while DR has not moved off 7. Most of that is link-vendor spam, and every Tier-1 peer shows the same pattern in the same narrow band. DR is the more trustworthy line on this page.

Domain Rating History
Monthly DR (0–100). Last point overridden with current point-in-time DR.
Referring Domains Growth (log)
14-month refdomain trajectory. The May–Jul 2026 jump is broad across the peer set.

Organic Traffic Trends

US organic traffic on a log scale, monthly through July 2026 plus a 10 August point. Star RRG is the standout riser in the peer tier, climbing from ~118 to 1,252 visits/mo on box-truck and car-hauler blog content. Milepost bottomed at 53 visits in April and has climbed back to 231. Progressive, The Hartford, GEICO and Insureon sit far above on their own plane, which is why the axis is logarithmic.

US Organic Traffic — Monthly (log scale)
All 15 domains on a log axis.

Traffic by Location

Milepost's organic traffic is effectively 100% US — all 231 visits/mo across 37 keywords — which is exactly right for a 30-state commercial-truck and commercial-auto agency. There is no international footprint to distribute, so this section is a confirmation check rather than an opportunity map.

Milepost is in an AI Overview for the first time

The dump truck insurance AI Overview cites milepostinsurance.com/vehicles-we-insure/commercial-dump-truck-insurance.html alongside Progressive, LogRock and FreightWaves. That page pulls just 1 organic visit/mo and ranks #1 on only a long-tail variant — proof that AIO citation is earned by answer structure, not by traffic or Domain Rating. Four of the ten tracked queries had an AIO a week ago and Milepost was in none of them.

Do next: reverse-engineer what the dump-truck page does right (definition in the first 60 words, coverage list, cost table) and port that structure onto the box truck, cargo van and limousine pages, which sit on AIO queries Milepost is not cited in.

Who is winning the AIOs now

Progressive Commercial is cited in all five live AI Overviews. GEICO is in two, The Hartford in two. Small sites keep getting in: Star RRG (DR 29) on box truck insurance, Business Ins. HQ (DR 1.3) on limousine insurance, Select Risk Group (DR 4) on owner operator insurance.

Also note: commercial auto insurance lost its AI Overview this week and owner operator insurance dropped Star RRG and Driver Advantage from its citation set. AIO presence and citation lists are volatile week to week — read a single cycle as a snapshot, not a trend.

Strategic Threats & Insights

The competitive picture distilled into prioritised, data-driven actions, ordered by severity. Severity reflects both the size of the gap and how fast it is moving — a Critical item is one that gets worse if nothing is done this month.

OpportunityNEW — Milepost earned its first AI Overview citation
Google's AI Overview for dump truck insurance now cites milepostinsurance.com/vehicles-we-insure/commercial-dump-truck-insurance.html, alongside Progressive, LogRock, FreightWaves and Colonial. That page draws 1 organic visit/mo on 2 keywords — so the citation was earned by page structure, not by traffic, rankings or Domain Rating. Milepost was cited in zero AI Overviews in every prior cycle.
Recommendation: Audit that page and document exactly what it does — opening definition, coverage breakdown, cost framing, FAQ block — then apply the same template to the box truck, cargo van and limousine pages. Those three sit on queries that return an AI Overview today and cite competitors instead.
CriticalGEICO's commercial-auto subfolder is still the page-level blueprint to beat
GEICO measured at the domain level does 4,128,991 US organic visits/mo on 73,947 keywords at DR 81.0. Inside that, the /commercial-auto-insurance/ subfolder alone does 33,376 visits/mo, its truck-insurance hub 15,285, its box-truck page 1,730 and its dump-truck page 1,027. Milepost's equivalents do 17 and 1. GEICO also has live pages for cargo van, food truck, cargo and non-trucking liability — the exact architecture Milepost is building.
Recommendation: Benchmark each Milepost vehicle page against GEICO's equivalent for depth, cost data and FAQ coverage before the next FPO ships. Do not benchmark against Progressive's homepage — the subfolder is the right comparison.
CriticalOrganic traffic is recovering but is still ~84% below a year ago
US organic traffic is 231 visits/mo on 37 ranking keywords, up 20% from 192 a week ago and up from the April floor of 53 — but down from 1,463 visits/mo in July 2025. Traffic value is $2.1K/mo. Paid still carries the pipeline: 153 paid keywords, 1,209 paid visits/mo, ~$10.1K/mo in equivalent paid traffic value.
Recommendation: The trend has turned, which is the important part — three consecutive weeks of organic gains. Keep the FPO cadence and resist reading one good week as recovery; the year-over-year hole is still 1,200 visits deep.
CriticalThe spam-link campaign got worse this week — disavow now
Referring domains went 405 → 444 and backlinks 636 → 705 in seven days, while DR stayed flat at 7.0. 28 of the top 40 referring domains (70%) are link-vendor PBNs, up from 27 of 40 (68%). The .shop network added rankboostly.shop on 2026-07-24, and the templated SEOExpress.org testimonial anchor now spans 220 referring domains — 199, then 213, now 220 across three cycles.
Recommendation: File the Google disavow this month using the flagged list in the Backlinks section, then re-check monthly. This is an active, growing campaign, not a historical artifact. Referring-domain growth on this profile is noise, not authority.
OpportunityStar RRG proves the model: DR 29, 1,252 visits/mo, all of it blog content
Star RRG now does 1,252 US visits/mo on 214 keywords at DR 29.0 — up from 118 visits at the start of the tracked window. Its single box-truck blog post pulls 390 visits/mo on 21 keywords and is cited in the box-truck AI Overview; its new-authority post pulls 115 on 26 keywords; its car-hauler post 83 on 20. Every one of those targets a KD-under-25 term.
Recommendation: This is the most replicable playbook on the board and it is working at a Domain Rating Milepost can reach. One post per vehicle type and per compliance question, each on a KD-under-25 term. Mirror the structure, not the copy.
WarningAI Overviews are volatile — do not read one cycle as a trend
Five of ten tracked queries return an AI Overview, the same count as last cycle, but the set changed. commercial auto insurance lost its AI Overview this week. owner operator insurance kept its AIO but dropped Star RRG and Driver Advantage from the citation list and added OOIDA, TruckSmarter and Select Risk Group. Progressive is cited in all five; GEICO and The Hartford in two each.
Recommendation: Track AIO presence and citations every cycle, but report movement over three or more cycles. A domain gaining or losing a citation in a single week is normal churn, not a program result.
OpportunityThe cargo-van page is now Milepost's second-biggest asset
/vehicles-we-insure/commercial-cargo-van-insurance.html pulls 64 visits/mo on 7 keywords, second only to the new-authority article at 85 visits/mo on 13 keywords. Together those two URLs are 65% of all site organic traffic. The new-authority article was 58% of the total by itself a week ago, so the concentration risk is easing as a second page starts to carry weight.
Recommendation: Two producing pages is not a program. Build the new-authority hub — cost, filings, timeline, state permits, FAQs — with the vehicle pages interlinked beneath it, and treat the cargo-van page as the template for the next three vehicle builds.
WarningRJS Truck Insurance collapsed from 2,348 visits to 55 — last cycle's caveat was right
RJS now shows 55 US visits/mo and $326 in traffic value, down from 2,348 visits and $54.8K a week ago. As flagged last cycle, 98.5% of that came from one page ranking on a single term, single truck insurance. That page now pulls 13 visits/mo.
Recommendation: Keep ignoring RJS as a strategic threat, and treat this as the standing warning about single-keyword artifacts anywhere in this dashboard. Still worth targeting single truck insurance — the term is clearly under-defended.
WarningbiBERK is a Berkshire sibling in the same auctions — coordinate, don't compete
biBERK does 95,934 US organic visits/mo on 3,659 keywords at DR 59.0, including a commercial-auto page at 2,394 visits/mo and a general-liability page at 4,023. It is simultaneously a paid-search rival, a Berkshire sibling, and an appointed carrier Milepost can quote GL, property and workers' comp through.
Recommendation: Do not build GL, property or workers-comp content that duplicates biBERK's ranking pages. Point that intent at the partnership and keep Milepost's organic surface on commercial auto, where biBERK is comparatively thin.
WarningPeer referring-domain counts are still clustered in a suspicious band
Tier-1 peers all sit between 415 and 570 referring domains — Milepost 444, 1st Guard 531, Star RRG 569, TWG 510, RJS 528, Driver Advantage 457, JDW 437, Business Ins. HQ 428, New Authority 415 — on wildly different content volumes and traffic levels. Unrelated domains do not converge on the same link count by accident.
Recommendation: Do not present the referring-domain chart to the client as competitive link-building momentum. Domain Rating is the more reliable authority signal in this set, and DR barely moved for anyone this cycle.
WarningRank-tracker: more keywords visible, fewer in the top 10
Two numbers moved in opposite directions in the week of Aug 3–9. The count of keywords ranking anywhere in the top 100 rose 116 → 127 — more of the tracked set is now visible at all. But top-10 keywords fell 37 → 28 and top-3 fell 12 → 11, and the average position across ranking keywords slipped 37.5 → 41.8 because the new entrants came in deep. The livery cluster gave back ground (executive transport insurance 1.0 → 72.0, uber black commercial insurance 37.6 → 100) while box-truck and passenger-van terms entered (box truck insurance requirements 100 → 5.9, how much is box truck insurance 100 → 23.6).
Recommendation: Report the top-10 count and the cluster story, not the average position — the average is being dragged by keywords that just entered the top 100 at position 60–90, which is progress, not decline. The Uber Black / livery sub-cluster has now swung wildly three cycles running; treat its rankings as unstable.
